127	class PassageManager:
128	    def __init__(
129	        self, passage_sources: list[dict[str, Any]], metadata_file_path: Optional[str] = None
130	    ):
131	        self.offset_maps: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
132	        self.passage_files: dict[str, str] = {}
133	        # Avoid materializing a single gigantic global map to reduce memory
134	        # footprint on very large corpora (e.g., 60M+ passages). Instead, keep
135	        # per-shard maps and do a lightweight per-shard lookup on demand.
136	        self._total_count: int = 0
137	        self.filter_engine = MetadataFilterEngine()  # Initialize filter engine
138	
139	        # Derive index base name for standard sibling fallbacks, e.g., <index_name>.passages.*
140	        index_name_base = None
141	        if metadata_file_path:
142	            meta_name = Path(metadata_file_path).name
143	            if meta_name.endswith(".meta.json"):
144	                index_name_base = meta_name[: -len(".meta.json")]
145	
146	        for source in passage_sources:
147	            assert source["type"] == "jsonl", "only jsonl is supported"
148	            passage_file = source.get("path", "")
149	            index_file = source.get("index_path", "")  # .idx file
150	
151	            # Fix path resolution - relative paths should be relative to metadata file directory
152	            def _resolve_candidates(
153	                primary: str,
154	                relative_key: str,
155	                default_name: Optional[str],
156	                source_dict: dict[str, Any],
157	            ) -> list[Path]:
158	                """
159	                Build an ordered list of candidate paths. For relative paths specified in
160	                metadata, prefer resolution relative to the metadata file directory first,
161	                then fall back to CWD-based resolution, and finally to conventional
162	                sibling defaults (e.g., <index_base>.passages.idx / .jsonl).
163	                """
164	                candidates: list[Path] = []
165	                # 1) Primary path
166	                if primary:
167	                    p = Path(primary)
168	                    if p.is_absolute():
169	                        candidates.append(p)
170	                    else:
171	                        # Prefer metadata-relative resolution for relative paths
172	                        if metadata_file_path:
173	                            candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / p)
174	                        # Also consider CWD-relative as a fallback for legacy layouts
175	                        candidates.append(Path.cwd() / p)
176	                # 2) metadata-relative explicit relative key (if present)
177	                if metadata_file_path and source_dict.get(relative_key):
178	                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / source_dict[relative_key])
179	                # 3) metadata-relative standard sibling filename
180	                if metadata_file_path and default_name:
181	                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / default_name)
182	                return candidates
183	
184	            # Build candidate lists and pick first existing; otherwise keep last candidate for error message
185	            idx_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.idx" if index_name_base else None
186	            idx_candidates = _resolve_candidates(
187	                index_file, "index_path_relative", idx_default, source
188	            )
189	            pas_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.jsonl" if index_name_base else None
190	            pas_candidates = _resolve_candidates(passage_file, "path_relative", pas_default, source)
191	
192	            def _pick_existing(cands: list[Path]) -> str:
193	                for c in cands:
194	                    if c.exists():
195	                        return str(c.resolve())
196	                # Fallback to last candidate (best guess) even if not exists; will error below
197	                return str(cands[-1].resolve()) if cands else ""
198	
199	            index_file = _pick_existing(idx_candidates)
200	            passage_file = _pick_existing(pas_candidates)
201	
202	            if not Path(index_file).exists():
203	                raise FileNotFoundError(f"Passage index file not found: {index_file}")
204	
205	            with open(index_file, "rb") as f:
206	                offset_map: dict[str, int] = pickle.load(f)
207	                self.offset_maps[passage_file] = offset_map
208	                self.passage_files[passage_file] = passage_file
209	                self._total_count += len(offset_map)
210	
211	    def get_passage(self, passage_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
212	        # Fast path: check each shard map (there are typically few shards).
213	        # This avoids building a massive combined dict while keeping lookups
214	        # bounded by the number of shards.
215	        for passage_file, offset_map in self.offset_maps.items():
216	            try:
217	                offset = offset_map[passage_id]
218	                with open(passage_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
219	                    f.seek(offset)
220	                    return json.loads(f.readline())
221	            except KeyError:
222	                continue
223	        raise KeyError(f"Passage ID not found: {passage_id}")

225	    def filter_search_results(
226	        self,
227	        search_results: list[SearchResult],
228	        metadata_filters: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Union[str, int, float, bool, list]]]],
229	    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
230	        """
231	        Apply metadata filters to search results.
232	
233	        Args:
234	            search_results: List of SearchResult objects
235	            metadata_filters: Filter specifications to apply
236	
237	        Returns:
238	            Filtered list of SearchResult objects
239	        """
240	        if not metadata_filters:
241	            return search_results
242	
243	        logger.debug(f"Applying metadata filters to {len(search_results)} results")
244	
245	        # Convert SearchResult objects to dictionaries for the filter engine
246	        result_dicts = []
247	        for result in search_results:
248	            result_dicts.append(
249	                {
250	                    "id": result.id,
251	                    "score": result.score,
252	                    "text": result.text,
253	                    "metadata": result.metadata,
254	                }
255	            )
256	
257	        # Apply filters using the filter engine
258	        filtered_dicts = self.filter_engine.apply_filters(result_dicts, metadata_filters)
259	
260	        # Convert back to SearchResult objects
261	        filtered_results = []
262	        for result_dict in filtered_dicts:
263	            filtered_results.append(
264	                SearchResult(
265	                    id=result_dict["id"],
266	                    score=result_dict["score"],
267	                    text=result_dict["text"],
268	                    metadata=result_dict["metadata"],
269	                )
270	            )
271	
272	        logger.debug(f"Filtered results: {len(filtered_results)} remaining")
273	        return filtered_results
274	
275	    def __len__(self) -> int:
276	        return self._total_count

Now I understand how the LEANN library works. I can see that `PassageManager` is used to manage passages and has an `offset_maps` dictionary that tracks passage IDs. Let me implement the complete function:

```python
# function_implementation_file

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import PassageManager
from pathlib import Path
import json

def get_passage_statistics(
    index_path: str
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Get statistics about passages in an index.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        
    Returns:
        Dictionary containing:
        {
            "total_passages": total number of passages,
            "passages_with_metadata": number of passages that have metadata,
            "passages_without_metadata": number of passages without metadata,
            "average_text_length": average length of passage texts
        }
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index metadata file is not found
    """
    # Construct metadata file path
    meta_path = f"{index_path}.meta.json"
    
    # Check if metadata file exists
    if not Path(meta_path).exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Index metadata file not found at {meta_path}"
        )
    
    # Load metadata
    with open(meta_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        meta_data = json.load(f)
    
    # Initialize PassageManager to access passages
    passage_manager = PassageManager(
        meta_data.get("passage_sources", []),
        metadata_file_path=meta_path
    )
    
    # Get total number of passages
    total_passages = len(passage_manager)
    
    # Initialize counters
    passages_with_metadata = 0
    passages_without_metadata = 0
    total_text_length = 0
    
    # Iterate through all passages to gather statistics
    for passage_file, offset_map in passage_manager.offset_maps.items():
        for passage_id in offset_map.keys():
            try:
                passage_data = passage_manager.get_passage(passage_id)
                
                # Check metadata
                metadata = passage_data.get("metadata", {})
                if metadata and len(metadata) > 0:
                    passages_with_metadata += 1
                else:
                    passages_without_metadata += 1
                
                # Add text length
                text = passage_data.get("text", "")
                total_text_length += len(text)
                
            except KeyError:
                # Skip if passage not found
                continue
    
    # Calculate average text length
    average_text_length = total_text_length / total_passages if total_passages > 0 else 0.0
    
    return {
        "total_passages": total_passages,
        "passages_with_metadata": passages_with_metadata,
        "passages_without_metadata": passages_without_metadata,
        "average_text_length": average_text_length
    }
```

This implementation:

1. **Constructs the metadata file path** by appending `.meta.json` to the `index_path`
2. **Checks if the metadata file exists** and raises `FileNotFoundError` if not found
3. **Loads the metadata** from the JSON file
4. **Initializes PassageManager** using the passage sources from metadata
5. **Gets total passages** using `len(passage_manager)` which returns `_total_count`
6. **Iterates through all passages** using the `offset_maps` from PassageManager to:
   - Count passages with and without metadata (checking if metadata dict is non-empty)
   - Calculate total text length
7. **Calculates average text length** by dividing total text length by total passages
8. **Returns a dictionary** with all the requested statistics

The function properly handles the LEANN index structure and uses the PassageManager API to access passage data efficiently.

```python
# function_implementation_file

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from pathlib import Path
from leann.api import LeannSearcher, SearchResult

def search_with_custom_scoring(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    score_multiplier: float = 1.0,
    top_k: int = 10
) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """Search in an index and apply a custom score multiplier to all results.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        score_multiplier: Multiplier to apply to all scores (default: 1.0)
        top_k: Number of results to retrieve (default: 10)
        
    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects with adjusted scores
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index file is not found
        ValueError: If score_multiplier < 0
    """
    # Validate score_multiplier
    if score_multiplier < 0:
        raise ValueError("score_multiplier must be non-negative")
    
    # Check if index file exists - this will raise FileNotFoundError if not found
    meta_path = f"{index_path}.meta.json"
    if not Path(meta_path).exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Leann metadata file not found at {meta_path}")
    
    # Initialize the searcher - this will also raise FileNotFoundError if index is missing
    searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)
    
    # Perform the search
    results = searcher.search(query, top_k=top_k)
    
    # Apply custom score multiplier to all results
    adjusted_results = []
    for result in results:
        # Create a new SearchResult with the adjusted score
        adjusted_result = SearchResult(
            id=result.id,
            score=result.score * score_multiplier,
            text=result.text,
            metadata=result.metadata
        )
        adjusted_results.append(adjusted_result)
    
    # Clean up the searcher resources
    searcher.cleanup()
    
    return adjusted_results
```

2. ✅ Checks if the index file exists and raises `FileNotFoundError` if not found

4. ✅ Performs a search with the given query and `top_k` parameter
5. ✅ Applies the custom score multiplier to all search results
6. ✅ Returns a list of `SearchResult` objects with adjusted scores
7. ✅ Properly cleans up resources after use

The function processes the Path to the LEANN index file, handles search query text strings, and returns a list of search result objects with adjusted scores as required.

def build_index_with_metadata_template(
    documents: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    index_path: str,
    metadata_template: Dict[str, Any] = None,
    backend_name: str = "hnsw"
) -> str:
    """Build a LEANN index and apply a metadata template to all documents.
    
    Args:
        documents: List of document dictionaries, each containing 'text' and optional 'metadata'
        index_path: Path where the index will be saved
        metadata_template: Optional metadata template to merge with each document's metadata (default: None)
        backend_name: Backend name for the index (default: "hnsw")
        
    Returns:
        Path to the built index file
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If documents list is empty
    """
    if not documents:
        raise ValueError("documents list cannot be empty")
    
    builder = LeannBuilder(backend_name=backend_name)
    
    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.get("text", "")
        if not text or not isinstance(text, str):
            continue
        
        # Merge template metadata with document metadata
        doc_metadata = doc.get("metadata", {})
        if metadata_template:
            merged_metadata = {**metadata_template, **doc_metadata}
        else:
            merged_metadata = doc_metadata
        
        if merged_metadata:
            builder.add_text(text, metadata=merged_metadata)
        else:
            builder.add_text(text)
    
    # Ensure parent directory exists
    index_path_obj = Path(index_path)
    index_path_obj.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    builder.build_index(index_path)
    return index_path

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannBuilder
from pathlib import Path

def build_index_with_metadata_template(
    documents: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    index_path: str,
    metadata_template: Dict[str, Any] = None,
    backend_name: str = "hnsw"
) -> str:
    """Build a LEANN index and apply a metadata template to all documents.

    Args:
        documents: List of document dictionaries, each containing 'text' and optional 'metadata'
        index_path: Path where the index will be saved
        metadata_template: Optional metadata template to merge with each document's metadata (default: None)
        backend_name: Backend name for the index (default: "hnsw")
    
    Returns:
        Path to the built index file
    
    Raises:
        ValueError: If documents list is empty
    """
    # Validate input
    if not documents:
        raise ValueError("documents list cannot be empty")
    
    # Initialize the builder
    builder = LeannBuilder(backend_name=backend_name)
    
    # Process each document
    for doc in documents:
        # Get the text from the document
        text = doc.get('text', '')
        
        # Start with document's existing metadata (if any)
        metadata = doc.get('metadata', {}).copy()
        
        # Merge with metadata template if provided
        if metadata_template:
            # Template values are applied first, then overridden by document-specific metadata
            merged_metadata = metadata_template.copy()
            merged_metadata.update(metadata)
            metadata = merged_metadata
        
        # Add the text with merged metadata to the builder
        builder.add_text(text, metadata=metadata)
    
    # Build the index
    builder.build_index(index_path)
    
    # Return the path to the built index
    return index_path
```

1. **Validates input**: Raises `ValueError` with the exact error message "documents list cannot be empty" when the documents list is empty
2. **Initializes LeannBuilder**: Creates a builder instance with the specified backend (default: "hnsw")
3. **Processes documents**: Iterates through each document:
   - Extracts the 'text' field
   - Extracts the optional 'metadata' field
   - Merges the metadata_template with document-specific metadata (template first, then document metadata to allow overrides)
4. **Builds the index**: Calls `builder.build_index()` to create the index at the specified path
5. **Returns the path**: Returns the index_path string as specified

The metadata merging strategy ensures that:
- If `metadata_template` is provided, it's applied to all documents as a base
- Document-specific metadata can override template values
- If no template is provided, only document metadata is used

    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    extract_field: str,
    top_k: int = 10
) -> List[Any]:
    """Search in an index and extract unique values of a metadata field from results.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        extract_field: Metadata field name to extract values from
        top_k: Number of results to retrieve (default: 10)
    
    Returns:
        List of unique field values found in search results (order preserved by first occurrence)
    
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When index file is not found
    """
    try:
        # Initialize the searcher with the given index path
        searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)
        
        # Perform the search
        search_results = searcher.search(query=query, top_k=top_k)
        
        # Extract unique field values while preserving order
        seen = set()
        unique_values = []
        
        for result in search_results:
            # Get the value from metadata
            if extract_field in result.metadata:
                value = result.metadata[extract_field]
                
                # For hashable types, use set to check uniqueness
                # For unhashable types (like lists/dicts), check manually
                try:
                    if value not in seen:
                        seen.add(value)
                        unique_values.append(value)
                except TypeError:
                    # Handle unhashable types (lists, dicts, etc.)
                    if value not in unique_values:
                        unique_values.append(value)
        
        # Cleanup the searcher
        searcher.cleanup()

    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        # Re-raise FileNotFoundError with the original message

83	def compute_embeddings_via_server(chunks: list[str], model_name: str, port: int) -> np.ndarray:
84	    """Computes embeddings using sentence-transformers.
85	
86	    Args:
87	        chunks: List of text chunks to embed
88	        model_name: Name of the sentence transformer model
89	    """
90	    logger.info(
91	        f"Computing embeddings for {len(chunks)} chunks using SentenceTransformer model '{model_name}' (via embedding server)..."
92	    )
93	    import msgpack
94	    import numpy as np
95	    import zmq
96	
97	    # Connect to embedding server
98	    context = zmq.Context()
99	    socket = context.socket(zmq.REQ)
100	    socket.connect(f"tcp://localhost:{port}")
101	
102	    # Send chunks to server for embedding computation
103	    request = chunks
104	    socket.send(msgpack.packb(request))
105	
106	    # Receive embeddings from server
107	    response = socket.recv()
108	    embeddings_list = msgpack.unpackb(response)
109	
110	    # Convert back to numpy array
111	    embeddings = np.array(embeddings_list, dtype=np.float32)
112	
113	    socket.close()
114	    context.term()
115	
116	    return embeddings

127	class PassageManager:
128	    def __init__(
129	        self, passage_sources: list[dict[str, Any]], metadata_file_path: Optional[str] = None
130	    ):
131	        self.offset_maps: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
132	        self.passage_files: dict[str, str] = {}
133	        # Avoid materializing a single gigantic global map to reduce memory
134	        # footprint on very large corpora (e.g., 60M+ passages). Instead, keep
135	        # per-shard maps and do a lightweight per-shard lookup on demand.
136	        self._total_count: int = 0
137	        self.filter_engine = MetadataFilterEngine()  # Initialize filter engine
138	
139	        # Derive index base name for standard sibling fallbacks, e.g., <index_name>.passages.*
140	        index_name_base = None
141	        if metadata_file_path:
142	            meta_name = Path(metadata_file_path).name
143	            if meta_name.endswith(".meta.json"):
144	                index_name_base = meta_name[: -len(".meta.json")]
145	
146	        for source in passage_sources:
147	            assert source["type"] == "jsonl", "only jsonl is supported"
148	            passage_file = source.get("path", "")
149	            index_file = source.get("index_path", "")  # .idx file
150	
151	            # Fix path resolution - relative paths should be relative to metadata file directory
152	            def _resolve_candidates(
153	                primary: str,
154	                relative_key: str,
155	                default_name: Optional[str],
156	                source_dict: dict[str, Any],
157	            ) -> list[Path]:
158	                """
159	                Build an ordered list of candidate paths. For relative paths specified in
160	                metadata, prefer resolution relative to the metadata file directory first,
161	                then fall back to CWD-based resolution, and finally to conventional
162	                sibling defaults (e.g., <index_base>.passages.idx / .jsonl).
163	                """
164	                candidates: list[Path] = []
165	                # 1) Primary path
166	                if primary:
167	                    p = Path(primary)
168	                    if p.is_absolute():
169	                        candidates.append(p)
170	                    else:
171	                        # Prefer metadata-relative resolution for relative paths
172	                        if metadata_file_path:
173	                            candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / p)
174	                        # Also consider CWD-relative as a fallback for legacy layouts
175	                        candidates.append(Path.cwd() / p)
176	                # 2) metadata-relative explicit relative key (if present)
177	                if metadata_file_path and source_dict.get(relative_key):
178	                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / source_dict[relative_key])
179	                # 3) metadata-relative standard sibling filename
180	                if metadata_file_path and default_name:
181	                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / default_name)
182	                return candidates
183	
184	            # Build candidate lists and pick first existing; otherwise keep last candidate for error message
185	            idx_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.idx" if index_name_base else None
186	            idx_candidates = _resolve_candidates(
187	                index_file, "index_path_relative", idx_default, source
188	            )
189	            pas_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.jsonl" if index_name_base else None
190	            pas_candidates = _resolve_candidates(passage_file, "path_relative", pas_default, source)
191	
192	            def _pick_existing(cands: list[Path]) -> str:
193	                for c in cands:
194	                    if c.exists():
195	                        return str(c.resolve())
196	                # Fallback to last candidate (best guess) even if not exists; will error below
197	                return str(cands[-1].resolve()) if cands else ""
198	
199	            index_file = _pick_existing(idx_candidates)
200	            passage_file = _pick_existing(pas_candidates)
201	
202	            if not Path(index_file).exists():
203	                raise FileNotFoundError(f"Passage index file not found: {index_file}")
204	
205	            with open(index_file, "rb") as f:
206	                offset_map: dict[str, int] = pickle.load(f)
207	                self.offset_maps[passage_file] = offset_map
208	                self.passage_files[passage_file] = passage_file
209	                self._total_count += len(offset_map)
210	
211	    def get_passage(self, passage_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
212	        # Fast path: check each shard map (there are typically few shards).
213	        # This avoids building a massive combined dict while keeping lookups
214	        # bounded by the number of shards.
215	        for passage_file, offset_map in self.offset_maps.items():
216	            try:
217	                offset = offset_map[passage_id]
218	                with open(passage_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
219	                    f.seek(offset)
220	                    return json.loads(f.readline())
221	            except KeyError:
222	                continue
223	        raise KeyError(f"Passage ID not found: {passage_id}")

225	    def filter_search_results(
226	        self,
227	        search_results: list[SearchResult],
228	        metadata_filters: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Union[str, int, float, bool, list]]]],
229	    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
230	        """
231	        Apply metadata filters to search results.
232	
233	        Args:
234	            search_results: List of SearchResult objects
235	            metadata_filters: Filter specifications to apply
236	
237	        Returns:
238	            Filtered list of SearchResult objects
239	        """
240	        if not metadata_filters:
241	            return search_results
242	
243	        logger.debug(f"Applying metadata filters to {len(search_results)} results")
244	
245	        # Convert SearchResult objects to dictionaries for the filter engine
246	        result_dicts = []
247	        for result in search_results:
248	            result_dicts.append(
249	                {
250	                    "id": result.id,
251	                    "score": result.score,
252	                    "text": result.text,
253	                    "metadata": result.metadata,
254	                }
255	            )
256	
257	        # Apply filters using the filter engine
258	        filtered_dicts = self.filter_engine.apply_filters(result_dicts, metadata_filters)
259	
260	        # Convert back to SearchResult objects
261	        filtered_results = []
262	        for result_dict in filtered_dicts:
263	            filtered_results.append(
264	                SearchResult(
265	                    id=result_dict["id"],
266	                    score=result_dict["score"],
267	                    text=result_dict["text"],
268	                    metadata=result_dict["metadata"],
269	                )
270	            )
271	
272	        logger.debug(f"Filtered results: {len(filtered_results)} remaining")
273	        return filtered_results
274	
275	    def __len__(self) -> int:
276	        return self._total_count

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannSearcher, SearchResult

def search_and_extract_field_values(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    extract_field: str,
    top_k: int = 10
) -> List[Any]:
    """Search in an index and extract unique values of a metadata field from results.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        extract_field: Metadata field name to extract values from
        top_k: Number of results to retrieve (default: 10)
    
    Returns:
        List of unique field values found in search results (order preserved by first occurrence)
    
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When index file is not found
    """
    try:
        # Initialize the searcher with the given index path
        searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)
        
        # Perform the search
        search_results = searcher.search(query=query, top_k=top_k)
        
        # Extract unique field values while preserving order
        seen = set()
        unique_values = []
        
        for result in search_results:
            # Get the value from metadata
            if extract_field in result.metadata:
                value = result.metadata[extract_field]
                
                # For hashable types, use set to check uniqueness
                # For unhashable types (like lists/dicts), check manually
                try:
                    if value not in seen:
                        seen.add(value)
                        unique_values.append(value)
                except TypeError:
                    # Handle unhashable types (lists, dicts, etc.)
                    if value not in unique_values:
                        unique_values.append(value)
        
        # Cleanup the searcher
        searcher.cleanup()
        
        return unique_values
        
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        # Re-raise FileNotFoundError with the original message
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index file not found: {index_path}") from e
```

4. **Handles both hashable and unhashable types** (like lists or dictionaries) when checking for uniqueness
5. **Cleans up resources** by calling `searcher.cleanup()` to stop any embedding servers
6. **Handles FileNotFoundError** - the `LeannSearcher.__init__` already raises `FileNotFoundError` when the metadata file is not found, so we catch and re-raise it with a clear message

The function returns a list of unique values in the order they first appear in the search results.

) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Retrieve passages from an index filtered by text length.
    
    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        min_length: Minimum text length in characters (default: 0)
        max_length: Maximum text length in characters (default: None, no upper limit)
        
    Returns:
        List of passage dictionaries with text length within the specified range
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index metadata file is not found
        ValueError: If min_length < 0 or max_length < min_length
    """
    if min_length < 0:
        raise ValueError("min_length must be non-negative")
    
    if max_length is not None and max_length < min_length:
        raise ValueError("max_length must be >= min_length")
    
    meta_path = Path(f"{index_path}.meta.json")
    if not meta_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index metadata file not found: {meta_path}")
    
    with open(meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        meta_data = json.load(f)
    
    passage_sources = meta_data.get("passage_sources", [])
    passage_manager = PassageManager(passage_sources, metadata_file_path=str(meta_path))
    
    passages_path = Path(f"{index_path}.passages.jsonl")
    if not passages_path.exists():
        return []
    
    matching_passages = []
    
    with open(passages_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            passage_data = json.loads(line)
            
            text = passage_data.get("text", "")
            text_length = len(text)
            
            if text_length >= min_length:
                if max_length is None or text_length <= max_length:
                    matching_passages.append(passage_data)
    
    return matching_passages

    """

    # Collect filtered passages
    filtered_passages = []
    
    # Iterate through all passages in all shards
    for passage_file, offset_map in passage_manager.offset_maps.items():

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import PassageManager
from pathlib import Path
import json

def get_passages_by_text_length(
    index_path: str,
    min_length: int = 0,
    max_length: int = None
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Retrieve passages from an index filtered by text length.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        min_length: Minimum text length in characters (default: 0)
        max_length: Maximum text length in characters (default: None, no upper limit)
    
    Returns:
        List of passage dictionaries with text length within the specified range
    
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index metadata file is not found
        ValueError: If min_length < 0 or max_length < min_length
    """
    # Validate parameters
    if min_length < 0:
        raise ValueError("max_length must be >= min_length")
    
    if max_length is not None and max_length < min_length:
        raise ValueError("max_length must be >= min_length")
    
    # Construct metadata file path
    meta_path = f"{index_path}.meta.json"
    
    # Check if metadata file exists
    if not Path(meta_path).exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index metadata file not found at {meta_path}")
    
    # Load metadata
    with open(meta_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        meta_data = json.load(f)
    
    # Get passage sources
    passage_sources = meta_data.get("passage_sources", [])
    
    # Initialize PassageManager
    passage_manager = PassageManager(passage_sources, metadata_file_path=meta_path)
    
    # Collect filtered passages
    filtered_passages = []
    
    # Iterate through all passages in all shards
    for passage_file, offset_map in passage_manager.offset_maps.items():
        for passage_id in offset_map.keys():
            try:
                # Retrieve the passage
                passage = passage_manager.get_passage(passage_id)
                text = passage.get("text", "")
                text_length = len(text)
                
                # Apply length filters
                if text_length >= min_length:
                    if max_length is None or text_length <= max_length:
                        filtered_passages.append(passage)
            except KeyError:
                # Skip passages that cannot be retrieved
                continue
    
    return filtered_passages

670	            )

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannSearcher, SearchResult

def search_with_result_expansion(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    expand_by_field: str,
    expansion_count: int = 1,
    top_k: int = 10
) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """Search in an index and expand results by including additional results with matching field values.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        expand_by_field: Metadata field name to use for expansion
        expansion_count: Number of additional results to include per unique field value (default: 1)
        top_k: Number of initial results to retrieve (default: 10)

    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects including expanded results

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index file is not found
        ValueError: If expansion_count < 0
    """
    # Validate expansion_count
    if expansion_count < 0:
        raise ValueError("expansion_count must be non-negative")

    # Initialize the searcher (this will raise FileNotFoundError if index doesn't exist)
    try:
        searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index file not found at: {index_path}")

    # Perform initial search
    initial_results = searcher.search(query, top_k=top_k)

    # If expansion_count is 0 or no results, return initial results
    if expansion_count == 0 or not initial_results:
        return initial_results

    # Track results and their IDs to avoid duplicates
    seen_ids = {result.id for result in initial_results}
    all_results = list(initial_results)

    # Collect unique field values from initial results
    field_values_map: Dict[Any, List[SearchResult]] = {}
    for result in initial_results:
        if expand_by_field in result.metadata:
            field_value = result.metadata[expand_by_field]
            if field_value not in field_values_map:
                field_values_map[field_value] = []
            field_values_map[field_value].append(result)

    # For each unique field value, find additional matching documents
    for field_value in field_values_map.keys():
        # Create metadata filter for this field value
        metadata_filters = {
            expand_by_field: {"==": field_value}
        }

        # Search for documents matching this field value
        # Request more results to ensure we get enough after filtering out duplicates
        expanded_search_results = searcher.search(
            query,
            top_k=top_k * 3,  # Get more results to account for duplicates
            metadata_filters=metadata_filters
        )

        # Add up to expansion_count new results for this field value
        added_count = 0
        for expanded_result in expanded_search_results:
            # Skip if already in results
            if expanded_result.id in seen_ids:
                continue

            # Add this new result

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannSearcher, SearchResult

def search_with_result_expansion(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    expand_by_field: str,
    expansion_count: int = 1,
    top_k: int = 10
) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """Search in an index and expand results by including additional results with matching field values.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        expand_by_field: Metadata field name to use for expansion
        expansion_count: Number of additional results to include per unique field value (default: 1)
        top_k: Number of initial results to retrieve (default: 10)

    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects including expanded results

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index file is not found
        ValueError: If expansion_count < 0
    """
    # Validate expansion_count
    if expansion_count < 0:
        raise ValueError("expansion_count must be non-negative")

    # Initialize the searcher (this will raise FileNotFoundError if index doesn't exist)
    try:
        searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index file not found at: {index_path}")

    # Perform initial search
    initial_results = searcher.search(query, top_k=top_k)

    # If expansion_count is 0 or no results, return initial results
    if expansion_count == 0 or not initial_results:
        return initial_results

    # Track results and their IDs to avoid duplicates
    seen_ids = {result.id for result in initial_results}
    all_results = list(initial_results)

    # Collect unique field values from initial results
    field_values_map: Dict[Any, List[SearchResult]] = {}
    for result in initial_results:
        if expand_by_field in result.metadata:
            field_value = result.metadata[expand_by_field]
            if field_value not in field_values_map:
                field_values_map[field_value] = []
            field_values_map[field_value].append(result)

    # For each unique field value, find additional matching documents
    for field_value in field_values_map.keys():
        # Create metadata filter for this field value
        metadata_filters = {
            expand_by_field: {"==": field_value}
        }

        # Search for documents matching this field value
        # Request more results to ensure we get enough after filtering out duplicates
        expanded_search_results = searcher.search(
            query,
            top_k=top_k * 3,  # Get more results to account for duplicates
            metadata_filters=metadata_filters
        )

        # Add up to expansion_count new results for this field value
        added_count = 0
        for expanded_result in expanded_search_results:
            # Skip if already in results
            if expanded_result.id in seen_ids:
                continue

            # Add this new result
            all_results.append(expanded_result)
            seen_ids.add(expanded_result.id)
            added_count += 1

            # Stop when we've added enough for this field value
            if added_count >= expansion_count:
                break

    # Clean up the searcher
    searcher.cleanup()

    return all_results
```

3. **Initial Search**: Performs the initial search using `searcher.search(query, top_k=top_k)`.

4. **Result Expansion Logic**:
   - Collects unique values of the `expand_by_field` from initial results
   - For each unique field value, performs an additional filtered search using the `metadata_filters` parameter
   - Uses the `{"==": value}` operator syntax supported by LEANN's metadata filtering
   - Adds up to `expansion_count` new results per unique field value
   - Tracks seen IDs to avoid duplicates

5. **Cleanup**: Properly cleans up the searcher resources using `searcher.cleanup()`.

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import compute_embeddings
import numpy as np


def compute_text_similarity_matrix(
    texts: List[str],
    model_name: str = "facebook/contriever",
    mode: str = "sentence-transformers"
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Compute pairwise similarity matrix for a list of texts using embeddings.
    
    Args:
        texts: List of text strings to compute similarities for
        model_name: Name of the embedding model to use (default: "facebook/contriever")
        mode: Embedding backend mode (default: "sentence-transformers")
        
    Returns:
        NumPy array of shape (len(texts), len(texts)) containing pairwise cosine similarities
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If texts list is empty
    """
    if not texts:
        raise ValueError("texts list cannot be empty")
    
    # Compute embeddings for all texts
    embeddings = compute_embeddings(
        chunks=texts,
        model_name=model_name,
        mode=mode,
        use_server=False,
        is_build=False
    )
    
    embeddings_array = np.array(embeddings)
    n = len(texts)
    similarity_matrix = np.zeros((n, n))
    
    # Compute pairwise cosine similarities
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            emb_i = embeddings_array[i]
            emb_j = embeddings_array[j]
            
            dot_product = np.dot(emb_i, emb_j)
            norm_i = np.linalg.norm(emb_i)
            norm_j = np.linalg.norm(emb_j)
            
            if norm_i > 0 and norm_j > 0:
                similarity = dot_product / (norm_i * norm_j)
                # Clip to valid range [-1, 1] to handle floating point precision issues
                similarity = np.clip(similarity, -1.0, 1.0)
            else:
                similarity = 0.0
            
            similarity_matrix[i, j] = similarity
    
    return similarity_matrix

def compute_text_similarity_matrix(
    texts: List[str],
    model_name: str = "facebook/contriever",
    mode: str = "sentence-transformers"
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Compute pairwise similarity matrix for a list of texts using embeddings.

    Args:
        texts: List of text strings to compute similarities for
        model_name: Name of the embedding model to use (default: "facebook/contriever")
        mode: Embedding backend mode (default: "sentence-transformers")

    Returns:
        NumPy array of shape (len(texts), len(texts)) containing pairwise cosine similarities

    Raises:
        ValueError: If texts list is empty
    """
    # Validate input
    if not texts:
        raise ValueError("texts list cannot be empty")

    # Compute embeddings for all texts
    # use_server=False ensures direct computation without requiring an embedding server
    embeddings = compute_embeddings(
        chunks=texts,
        model_name=model_name,
        mode=mode,
        use_server=False
    )

    # Normalize embeddings for cosine similarity computation
    # After normalization, dot product equals cosine similarity
    norms = np.linalg.norm(embeddings, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    # Avoid division by zero
    norms = np.where(norms == 0, 1, norms)
    normalized_embeddings = embeddings / norms

    # Compute pairwise cosine similarities using matrix multiplication
    # Shape: (len(texts), embedding_dim) @ (embedding_dim, len(texts)) = (len(texts), len(texts))
    similarity_matrix = np.dot(normalized_embeddings, normalized_embeddings.T)

98	    context = zmq.Context()
99	    socket = context.socket(zmq.REQ)
100	    socket.connect(f"tcp://localhost:{port}")
101	
102	    # Send chunks to server for embedding computation
103	    request = chunks
104	    socket.send(msgpack.packb(request))

106	    # Receive embeddings from server

111	    embeddings = np.array(embeddings_list, dtype=np.float32)

126	def truncate_to_token_limit(texts: list[str], token_limit: int) -> list[str]:
127	    """
128	    Truncate texts to fit within token limit using tiktoken.
129	
130	    Args:
131	        texts: List of text strings to truncate
132	        token_limit: Maximum number of tokens allowed
133	
134	    Returns:
135	        List of truncated texts (same length as input)
136	    """
137	    if not texts:
138	        return []
139	
140	    # Use tiktoken with cl100k_base encoding
141	    enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
142	
143	    truncated_texts = []
144	    truncation_count = 0
145	    total_tokens_removed = 0
146	    max_original_length = 0
147	
148	    for i, text in enumerate(texts):
149	        tokens = enc.encode(text)
150	        original_length = len(tokens)
151	
152	        if original_length <= token_limit:
153	            # Text is within limit, keep as is
154	            truncated_texts.append(text)
155	        else:
156	            # Truncate to token_limit
157	            truncated_tokens = tokens[:token_limit]
158	            truncated_text = enc.decode(truncated_tokens)
159	            truncated_texts.append(truncated_text)
160	
161	            # Track truncation statistics
162	            truncation_count += 1
163	            tokens_removed = original_length - token_limit
164	            total_tokens_removed += tokens_removed
165	            max_original_length = max(max_original_length, original_length)
166	
167	            # Log individual truncation at WARNING level (first few only)
168	            if truncation_count <= 3:
169	                logger.warning(
170	                    f"Text {i + 1} truncated: {original_length} → {token_limit} tokens "
171	                    f"({tokens_removed} tokens removed)"
172	                )
173	            elif truncation_count == 4:
174	                logger.warning("Further truncation warnings suppressed...")
175	
176	    # Log summary at INFO level
177	    if truncation_count > 0:
178	        logger.warning(
179	            f"Truncation summary: {truncation_count}/{len(texts)} texts truncated "
180	            f"(removed {total_tokens_removed} tokens total, longest was {max_original_length} tokens)"
181	        )
182	    else:
183	        logger.debug(
184	            f"No truncation needed - all {len(texts)} texts within {token_limit} token limit"
185	        )
186	
187	    return truncated_texts

from typing import List
from leann.api import compute_embeddings
import numpy as np

def compute_text_similarity_matrix(
    texts: List[str],
    model_name: str = "facebook/contriever",
    mode: str = "sentence-transformers"
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Compute pairwise similarity matrix for a list of texts using embeddings.

    Args:
        texts: List of text strings to compute similarities for
        model_name: Name of the embedding model to use (default: "facebook/contriever")
        mode: Embedding backend mode (default: "sentence-transformers")

    Returns:
        NumPy array of shape (len(texts), len(texts)) containing pairwise cosine similarities

    Raises:
        ValueError: If texts list is empty
    """
    # Validate input
    if not texts:
        raise ValueError("texts list cannot be empty")

    # Compute embeddings for all texts
    # use_server=False ensures direct computation without requiring an embedding server
    embeddings = compute_embeddings(
        chunks=texts,
        model_name=model_name,
        mode=mode,
        use_server=False
    )

    # Normalize embeddings for cosine similarity computation
    # After normalization, dot product equals cosine similarity
    norms = np.linalg.norm(embeddings, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    # Avoid division by zero
    norms = np.where(norms == 0, 1, norms)
    normalized_embeddings = embeddings / norms

    # Compute pairwise cosine similarities using matrix multiplication
    # Shape: (len(texts), embedding_dim) @ (embedding_dim, len(texts)) = (len(texts), len(texts))
    similarity_matrix = np.dot(normalized_embeddings, normalized_embeddings.T)

    return similarity_matrix

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannBuilder, LeannSearcher
from pathlib import Path

def build_and_verify_searchable(
    documents: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    index_path: str,
    test_query: str = "test",
    backend_name: str = "hnsw"
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Build an index and verify it is searchable.

    Args:
        documents: List of document dictionaries, each containing 'text' and optional 'metadata'
        index_path: Path where the index will be saved
        test_query: Query string to test searchability (default: "test")
        backend_name: Backend name for the index (default: "hnsw")
        
    Returns:
        Dictionary containing:
        {
            "index_path": path to the built index,
            "is_searchable": boolean indicating if index is searchable,
            "test_results_count": number of results from test query
        }
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If documents list is empty
    """
    # Validate documents list
    if not documents:
        raise ValueError("documents list cannot be empty")
    
    # Initialize builder
    builder = LeannBuilder(backend_name=backend_name)
    
    # Add documents to the builder
    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.get('text', '')
        metadata = doc.get('metadata', {})
        builder.add_text(text=text, metadata=metadata)
    
    # Build the index
    builder.build_index(index_path=index_path)
    
    # Verify searchability by creating a searcher and performing a test query
    try:
        searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path=index_path)
        
        # Perform test search
        test_results = searcher.search(query=test_query, top_k=5)
        
        # Check if search was successful
        is_searchable = True
        test_results_count = len(test_results)
        
        # Cleanup
        searcher.cleanup()
        
    except Exception as e:
        # If search fails, index is not searchable
        is_searchable = False
        test_results_count = 0
    
    # Return result dictionary
    return {
        "index_path": index_path,
        "is_searchable": is_searchable,
        "test_results_count": test_results_count
    }
```

6. **Returns the required dictionary** - Contains `index_path`, `is_searchable` boolean, and `test_results_count`

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannSearcher, SearchResult

def search_with_minimum_field_value(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    field_name: str,
    min_value: float,
    top_k: int = 10
) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """Search in an index and filter results by minimum numeric metadata field value.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        field_name: Metadata field name containing numeric values
        min_value: Minimum field value threshold
        top_k: Number of results to retrieve (default: 10)

    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects with field values >= min_value

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When index file is not found
    """
    try:
        # Initialize the LeannSearcher with the provided index path
        searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)

        # Perform the search with the query and top_k
        search_results = searcher.search(query=query, top_k=top_k)

        # Filter results based on the minimum field value
        filtered_results = []
        for result in search_results:
            # Check if the field exists in metadata
            if field_name in result.metadata:
                field_value = result.metadata[field_name]

                # Convert to float if necessary and compare with min_value
                try:
                    if float(field_value) >= min_value:
                        filtered_results.append(result)
                except (ValueError, TypeError):
                    # Skip results where the field value cannot be converted to float
                    continue

        # Clean up resources
        searcher.cleanup()

        return filtered_results

    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        # Re-raise FileNotFoundError with more context
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index file not found at '{index_path}': {str(e)}")

import json


def get_passages_by_text_contains(
    index_path: str,
    search_text: str,
    case_sensitive: bool = False
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Retrieve passages from an index whose text contains a specific substring.
    
    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        search_text: Substring to search for in passage texts
        case_sensitive: Whether the search should be case-sensitive (default: False)
        
    Returns:
        List of passage dictionaries whose text contains the search_text
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index metadata file is not found
        ValueError: If search_text is empty
    """
    if not search_text:
        raise ValueError("search_text cannot be empty")
    
    meta_path = Path(f"{index_path}.meta.json")
    if not meta_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index metadata file not found: {meta_path}")
    
    with open(meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        meta_data = json.load(f)
    
    passage_sources = meta_data.get("passage_sources", [])
    passage_manager = PassageManager(passage_sources, metadata_file_path=str(meta_path))
    
    passages_path = Path(f"{index_path}.passages.jsonl")
    if not passages_path.exists():
        return []
    
    matching_passages = []
    
    with open(passages_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            passage_data = json.loads(line)
            
            text = passage_data.get("text", "")
            if case_sensitive:
                matches = search_text in text
            else:
                matches = search_text.lower() in text.lower()
            
            if matches:
                matching_passages.append(passage_data)
    
    return matching_passages

160	                metadata, prefer resolution relative to the metadata file directory first,
161	                then fall back to CWD-based resolution, and finally to conventional
162	                sibling defaults (e.g., <index_base>.passages.idx / .jsonl).
163	                """
164	                candidates: list[Path] = []
165	                # 1) Primary path
166	                if primary:
167	                    p = Path(primary)
168	                    if p.is_absolute():
169	                        candidates.append(p)
170	                    else:
171	                        # Prefer metadata-relative resolution for relative paths
172	                        if metadata_file_path:
173	                            candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / p)
174	                        # Also consider CWD-relative as a fallback for legacy layouts
175	                        candidates.append(Path.cwd() / p)
176	                # 2) metadata-relative explicit relative key (if present)
177	                if metadata_file_path and source_dict.get(relative_key):
178	                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / source_dict[relative_key])
179	                # 3) metadata-relative standard sibling filename
180	                if metadata_file_path and default_name:
181	                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / default_name)
182	                return candidates
183	
184	            # Build candidate lists and pick first existing; otherwise keep last candidate for error message
185	            idx_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.idx" if index_name_base else None
186	            idx_candidates = _resolve_candidates(
187	                index_file, "index_path_relative", idx_default, source
188	            )
189	            pas_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.jsonl" if index_name_base else None
190	            pas_candidates = _resolve_candidates(passage_file, "path_relative", pas_default, source)
191	
192	            def _pick_existing(cands: list[Path]) -> str:
193	                for c in cands:
194	                    if c.exists():
195	                        return str(c.resolve())
196	                # Fallback to last candidate (best guess) even if not exists; will error below
197	                return str(cands[-1].resolve()) if cands else ""
198	
199	            index_file = _pick_existing(idx_candidates)
200	            passage_file = _pick_existing(pas_candidates)
201	
202	            if not Path(index_file).exists():
203	                raise FileNotFoundError(f"Passage index file not found: {index_file}")
204	
205	            with open(index_file, "rb") as f:
206	                offset_map: dict[str, int] = pickle.load(f)
207	                self.offset_maps[passage_file] = offset_map
208	                self.passage_files[passage_file] = passage_file
209	                self._total_count += len(offset_map)

211	    def get_passage(self, passage_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
212	        # Fast path: check each shard map (there are typically few shards).
213	        # This avoids building a massive combined dict while keeping lookups
214	        # bounded by the number of shards.
215	        for passage_file, offset_map in self.offset_maps.items():
216	            try:
217	                offset = offset_map[passage_id]
218	                with open(passage_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
219	                    f.seek(offset)
220	                    return json.loads(f.readline())
221	            except KeyError:
222	                continue
223	        raise KeyError(f"Passage ID not found: {passage_id}")

661	        if not index_file.exists():

663	
664	        with open(meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
665	            meta = json.load(f)

667	        if backend_name != self.backend_name:
668	            raise ValueError(
669	                f"Index was built with backend '{backend_name}', cannot update with '{self.backend_name}'."
670	            )
671	
672	        meta_backend_kwargs = meta.get("backend_kwargs", {})
673	        index_is_compact = meta.get("is_compact", meta_backend_kwargs.get("is_compact", True))
674	        if index_is_compact:

680	            "distance_metric", self.backend_kwargs.get("distance_metric", "mips")
681	        ).lower()

683	            meta.get("is_pruned")

691

693	        for chunk in self.chunks:

```python
# function_implementation_file

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from pathlib import Path
import json

def get_passages_by_text_contains(
    index_path: str,
    search_text: str,
    case_sensitive: bool = False
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Retrieve passages from an index whose text contains a specific substring.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        search_text: Substring to search for in passage texts
        case_sensitive: Whether the search should be case-sensitive (default: False)
        
    Returns:
        List of passage dictionaries whose text contains the search_text
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index metadata file is not found
        ValueError: If search_text is empty
    """
    # Validate search_text
    if not search_text:
        raise ValueError("search_text cannot be empty")
    
    # Construct metadata file path
    index_path_obj = Path(index_path)
    if not index_path_obj.is_absolute():
        index_path_obj = index_path_obj.resolve()
    
    meta_path = Path(f"{index_path_obj}.meta.json")
    
    # Check if metadata file exists
    if not meta_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index metadata file not found at {meta_path}")
    
    # Load metadata
    with open(meta_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        meta_data = json.load(f)
    
    # Get passage sources
    passage_sources = meta_data.get('passage_sources', [])
    
    # Prepare search text based on case sensitivity
    search_key = search_text if case_sensitive else search_text.lower()
    
    # Collect matching passages
    matching_passages = []
    
    # Process each passage source
    for source in passage_sources:
        if source.get('type') != 'jsonl':
            continue
        
        # Resolve passage file path
        passage_file = source.get('path', '')
        
        # Try to resolve the path relative to metadata file directory
        if not Path(passage_file).is_absolute():
            # First try relative to metadata file
            passage_file_path = meta_path.parent / passage_file
            
            # If not found, try other locations
            if not passage_file_path.exists():
                # Try with standard naming convention
                index_name_base = meta_path.name[:-len('.meta.json')] if meta_path.name.endswith('.meta.json') else None
                if index_name_base:
                    passage_file_path = meta_path.parent / f"{index_name_base}.passages.jsonl"
        else:
            passage_file_path = Path(passage_file)
        
        # Check if passage file exists
        if not passage_file_path.exists():
            continue
        
        # Read through the JSONL file and search for matching passages
        with open(passage_file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                
                try:
                    passage = json.loads(line)
                    text = passage.get('text', '')
                    
                    # Check if text contains search_text
                    text_to_check = text if case_sensitive else text.lower()
                    
                    if search_key in text_to_check:
                        matching_passages.append(passage)
                
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    # Skip invalid JSON lines
                    continue
    
    return matching_passages
```

This implementation:

1. **Validates the search_text**: Raises `ValueError` with the exact message "search_text cannot be empty" if the search text is empty
2. **Processes the index path**: Resolves it to an absolute path
3. **Loads metadata**: Opens the `.meta.json` file and raises `FileNotFoundError` if it doesn't exist
4. **Resolves passage file paths**: Handles both absolute and relative paths, with fallback to standard naming conventions
5. **Searches through passages**: Reads each JSONL file line by line and checks if the text contains the search substring
6. **Handles case sensitivity**: Converts both the search text and passage text to lowercase when case_sensitive is False
7. **Returns matching passages**: Returns a list of passage dictionaries that contain the search text
8. **Handles errors gracefully**: Skips invalid JSON lines and continues processing

The function integrates well with the LEANN library's file structure and follows the same pattern used in the `PassageManager` class for resolving file paths.

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannSearcher, SearchResult
from collections import Counter


def search_and_get_top_field_values(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    field_name: str,
    top_n: int = 5,
    search_top_k: int = 20
) -> List[tuple]:
    """Search in an index and return the top N most common field values in results.
    
    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        field_name: Metadata field name to analyze
        top_n: Number of top values to return (default: 5)
        search_top_k: Number of results to retrieve for analysis (default: 20)
        
    Returns:
        List of tuples (field_value, count) sorted by count (descending), limited to top_n
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index file is not found
        ValueError: If top_n <= 0
    """
    if top_n <= 0:
        raise ValueError("top_n must be greater than 0")
    
    searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path=index_path)
    results = searcher.search(query, top_k=search_top_k)
    
    # Count field values
    counter = Counter()
    for result in results:
        metadata = result.metadata or {}
        field_value = metadata.get(field_name)
        if field_value is not None:
            counter[field_value] += 1
    
    # Get top N
    top_values = counter.most_common(top_n)
    return top_values

def search_and_get_top_field_values(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    field_name: str,
    top_n: int = 5,
    search_top_k: int = 20
) -> List[tuple]:
    """Search in an index and return the top N most common field values in results.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        field_name: Metadata field name to analyze
        top_n: Number of top values to return (default: 5)

    Returns:
        List of tuples (field_value, count) sorted by count (descending), limited to top_n
    
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index file is not found
        ValueError: If top_n <= 0
    """

    if top_n <= 0:
        raise ValueError("top_n must be greater than 0")
    
    # Check if index file exists
    meta_path = f"{index_path}.meta.json"
    if not Path(meta_path).exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index file not found at {index_path}")
    
    # Initialize the searcher

    # Extract field values from metadata

```python
from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannSearcher, SearchResult
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

def search_and_get_top_field_values(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    field_name: str,
    top_n: int = 5,
    search_top_k: int = 20
) -> List[tuple]:
    """Search in an index and return the top N most common field values in results.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        field_name: Metadata field name to analyze
        top_n: Number of top values to return (default: 5)
        search_top_k: Number of results to retrieve for analysis (default: 20)
    
    Returns:
        List of tuples (field_value, count) sorted by count (descending), limited to top_n
    
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index file is not found
        ValueError: If top_n <= 0
    """
    # Validate top_n parameter
    if top_n <= 0:
        raise ValueError("top_n must be greater than 0")
    
    # Check if index file exists
    meta_path = f"{index_path}.meta.json"
    if not Path(meta_path).exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index file not found at {index_path}")
    
    # Initialize the searcher
    try:
        searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index file not found at {index_path}")
    
    # Perform the search
    search_results: List[SearchResult] = searcher.search(query, top_k=search_top_k)
    
    # Extract field values from metadata
    field_values = []
    for result in search_results:
        if field_name in result.metadata:
            field_values.append(result.metadata[field_name])
    
    # Count occurrences of each field value
    value_counts = Counter(field_values)
    
    # Get top N most common values
    top_values = value_counts.most_common(top_n)
    
    # Clean up the searcher
    searcher.cleanup()
    
    return top_values
```

This implementation:

1. **Validates `top_n`**: Raises `ValueError` with the exact message "top_n must be greater than 0" when `top_n <= 0`
2. **Checks for index file**: Verifies that the `.meta.json` file exists, which is required by `LeannSearcher`, and raises `FileNotFoundError` if not found
3. **Initializes `LeannSearcher`**: Creates a searcher instance with the provided index path
4. **Performs search**: Uses the `search()` method to retrieve `search_top_k` results for the query
5. **Extracts field values**: Iterates through search results and extracts the specified field from metadata
6. **Counts occurrences**: Uses `Counter` from `collections` to count how many times each field value appears
7. **Returns top N**: Uses `Counter.most_common(top_n)` to get the top N most common values as tuples of `(field_value, count)`, sorted by count in descending order
8. **Cleans up**: Calls `cleanup()` to stop the embedding server and release resources

The function handles the requirements properly and follows the LEANN API patterns observed in the code.

83	def compute_embeddings_via_server(chunks: list[str], model_name: str, port: int) -> np.ndarray:
84	    """Computes embeddings using sentence-transformers.
85	
86	    Args:
87	        chunks: List of text chunks to embed
88	        model_name: Name of the sentence transformer model
89	    """
90	    logger.info(
91	        f"Computing embeddings for {len(chunks)} chunks using SentenceTransformer model '{model_name}' (via embedding server)..."
92	    )
93	    import msgpack
94	    import numpy as np
95	    import zmq
96	
97	    # Connect to embedding server
98	    context = zmq.Context()
99	    socket = context.socket(zmq.REQ)
100	    socket.connect(f"tcp://localhost:{port}")
101	
102	    # Send chunks to server for embedding computation
103	    request = chunks
104	    socket.send(msgpack.packb(request))
105	
106	    # Receive embeddings from server
107	    response = socket.recv()
108	    embeddings_list = msgpack.unpackb(response)
109	
110	    # Convert back to numpy array
111	    embeddings = np.array(embeddings_list, dtype=np.float32)
112	
113	    socket.close()
114	    context.term()
115	
116	    return embeddings

from leann.api import LeannBuilder, LeannSearcher

def build_index_and_search(
    documents: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    top_k: int = 5,
    backend_name: str = "hnsw"
) -> List[Any]:
    """Build an index and immediately perform a search on it.

    Args:
        documents: List of document dictionaries, each containing 'text' and optional 'metadata'
        index_path: Path where the index will be saved
        query: Search query string
        top_k: Number of results to retrieve (default: 5)
        backend_name: Backend name for the index (default: "hnsw")
    
    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects from the search
    
    Raises:
        ValueError: If documents list is empty or query is empty
    """
    # Validate inputs
    if not documents:
        raise ValueError("documents list cannot be empty")
    
    if not query or not query.strip():
        raise ValueError("query cannot be empty")
    
    # Create a builder instance
    builder = LeannBuilder(backend_name=backend_name)
    
    # Add documents to the builder
    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.get('text', '')
        metadata = doc.get('metadata', {})
        builder.add_text(text=text, metadata=metadata)
    
    # Build the index
    builder.build_index(index_path)
    
    # Create a searcher instance
    searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)
    
    # Perform the search
    results = searcher.search(query=query, top_k=top_k)
    
    # Clean up searcher resources
    searcher.cleanup()
    
    return results
```

8. **Returns results** - Returns a list of SearchResult objects containing id, score, text, and metadata

The function handles both required and optional metadata in documents, and returns structured SearchResult objects that contain all the relevant information from the search.

# function_implementation_file

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannSearcher, SearchResult

def search_with_field_requirement(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    required_field: str,
    top_k: int = 10
) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """Search in an index and only return results that have a specific metadata field.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        required_field: Metadata field name that must be present in results
        top_k: Number of results to retrieve (default: 10)
        
    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects that have the required field
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When index file is not found
    """
    try:
        # Initialize the searcher with the provided index path
        searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)
        
        # Perform the search
        results = searcher.search(query=query, top_k=top_k)
        
        # Filter results to only include those with the required metadata field
        filtered_results = [
            result for result in results
            if required_field in result.metadata
        ]
        
        # Cleanup resources
        searcher.cleanup()
        
        return filtered_results
        
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        # Re-raise FileNotFoundError with more context
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Index file not found at path: {index_path}. "
            f"Original error: {str(e)}"
        ) from e
```

Now I understand how the LEANN library works. Based on the API, I can see that:

1. `LeannSearcher` is the main class for searching
2. `SearchResult` is a dataclass with `id`, `score`, `text`, and `metadata` fields

Here's the complete implementation:

```python
# function_implementation_file

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannSearcher, SearchResult

def search_with_field_requirement(
    index_path: str,
    query: str,
    required_field: str,
    top_k: int = 10
) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """Search in an index and only return results that have a specific metadata field.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the LEANN index file
        query: Search query string
        required_field: Metadata field name that must be present in results
        top_k: Number of results to retrieve (default: 10)
        
    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects that have the required field
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When index file is not found
    """
    try:
        # Initialize the searcher with the provided index path
        searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path)
        
        # Perform the search
        results = searcher.search(query=query, top_k=top_k)
        
        # Filter results to only include those with the required metadata field
        filtered_results = [
            result for result in results
            if required_field in result.metadata
        ]
        
        # Cleanup resources
        searcher.cleanup()
        
        return filtered_results
        
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        # Re-raise FileNotFoundError with more context
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Index file not found at path: {index_path}. "
            f"Original error: {str(e)}"
        ) from e
```

This implementation:

1. **Creates a LeannSearcher instance** using the provided `index_path`
2. **Performs the search** using the `search()` method with the query and top_k parameters
3. **Filters results** to only include SearchResult objects that have the `required_field` in their metadata dictionary
4. **Cleans up resources** by calling `searcher.cleanup()` to stop any background embedding servers
5. **Handles FileNotFoundError** by catching it and re-raising with additional context about the index path

The function returns a list of `SearchResult` objects that satisfy the requirement of having the specified metadata field present.

from typing import List, Dict, Any
from leann.api import LeannBuilder
from pathlib import Path

def build_index_with_auto_metadata(
    texts: List[str],
    index_path: str,
    auto_metadata_func: callable = None,
    backend_name: str = "hnsw"
) -> str:
    """Build a LEANN index with automatically generated metadata for each text.

    Args:
        texts: List of text strings to index
        index_path: Path where the index will be saved
        auto_metadata_func: Optional function to generate metadata from text.
            Function signature: (text: str, index: int) -> Dict[str, Any]
            If None, no metadata is added
        backend_name: Backend name for the index (default: "hnsw")
    
    Returns:
        Path to the built index file
    
    Raises:
        ValueError: If texts list is empty
    """
    # Validate inputs
    if not texts:
        raise ValueError("texts list cannot be empty")
    
    # Create a LeannBuilder instance
    builder = LeannBuilder(
        backend_name=backend_name,
        embedding_model="facebook/contriever"
    )
    
    # Add texts with auto-generated metadata
    for idx, text in enumerate(texts):
        # Generate metadata if function is provided
        if auto_metadata_func is not None:
            metadata = auto_metadata_func(text, idx)
        else:
            metadata = {}
        
        # Ensure the metadata has an ID
        if "id" not in metadata:
            metadata["id"] = str(idx)
        
        # Add the text with metadata to the builder
        builder.add_text(text, metadata=metadata)
    
    # Build the index
    builder.build_index(index_path)
    
    # Return the path to the built index file
    return index_path

from typing import List, Dict, Any

def build_index_with_auto_metadata(
    texts: List[str],
    index_path: str,
    auto_metadata_func: callable = None,
    backend_name: str = "hnsw"
) -> str:
    """Build a LEANN index with automatically generated metadata for each text.

    Args:
        texts: List of text strings to index
        index_path: Path where the index will be saved
        auto_metadata_func: Optional function to generate metadata from text.
            Function signature: (text: str, index: int) -> Dict[str, Any]
